children: shares declined about 4% after releasing its third-quarter 2026 financial
For the quarter ended September 30, the Berkeley-based quantum computing company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.06 versus the consensus estimate of ($0.05).

Revenue for the third quarter declined 28% year over year to $1.41M, which was much less than the $3.52M estimate. It reported an operating loss of $33.2M versus the estimate calling for a loss of $29.1M. Its operating expenses increased 62% year over year to $34M, which was more than the $27.4M consensus.
For the full year, Rigetti expects revenue of $20M, which is less than the $22.6M estimate.

"Rigetti delivered meaningful progress during the third quarter across system performance, technology development and strategic execution," said Rigetti CEO Subodh Kulkarni. "Our Cepheus-1-108Q system achieved our goal of 99.5% median two-qubit gate fidelity, demonstrating continued performance improvement at the 100-plus-qubit level and further validating our chiplet-based approach to scaling superconducting quantum computers."

"Building on the progress achieved this quarter, our next major system objective is to demonstrate a 300-plus-qubit system with approximately 99.7% median two-qubit gate fidelity and gate speeds below 60 nanoseconds by mid-2028," he added.

title: Rigetti dips after Q3 financial results fall short of expectations
